## Airtable
The Airtable MCP Server provides tools to interact with Airtable bases.

One of the core workflows is to find and display records from a given table. For example, "Show me projects on the roadmap shipping this week".

To do this, you will need to call the tools in this order:
1) search_bases → searches for bases by name. Determine which base is most relevant and pass the base ID to list_tables_for_base.
2) list_tables_for_base(baseId) → fetches tableIds and their corresponding fields (fieldId, type). Use this to decide which tables and fields are relevant.
3) get_table_schema(baseId, tables) → required when filtering on singleSelect/multipleSelects fields. Fetches detailed field schema including choice IDs and names. Call this before filtering to get the correct choice IDs. Each table entry must include tableId and fieldIds.
4) (a) if available, use display_records_for_table(baseId, tableId, ...params) → displays records only from the relevant table(s). Use params to filter, sort, select fields, and paginate.
   (b) otherwise, use list_records_for_table(baseId, tableId, ...params) → lists records only from the relevant table(s). Use params to filter, sort, select fields, and paginate.

Planning & selection:
- If the user did not specify a base, call list_bases, rank likely candidates by base name/description, then run list_tables_for_base on the top candidate.

Interfaces and pages:
- If the user asks about interfaces, pages, or dashboards, read data through them with list_records_for_page or get_record_for_page. Call list_pages_for_base(baseId) first if needed to find the required parameters (e.g., pageId or interfaceId).
- Some bases may have permissionLevel "interfaceOnly" (or "none" in older responses), meaning the user has interface-only access (shared via specific interfaces, not as a full base collaborator). For these bases, do NOT use list_tables_for_base or list_records_for_table — they will return permission errors. Use the page-based tools above instead.

ID formats:
- Always operate on Airtable intern… [truncated]

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

{"number":11,"title":"Citation check: does the reference actually support the claim it's cited for?","body":"## Why

The deepest version of citation checking, and the one that catches sophisticated slop: real paper, correct metadata, real quote — cited for a claim it does not support.

## Scope

- For each (claim sentence, citation) pair with retrievable source text, ask an LLM whether the source supports, partially supports, is unrelated to, or contradicts the claim.
- Ground the judgment: require the model to return the supporting passage from the source, and drop any verdict whose quoted passage isn't actually in the retrieved text. No passage, no finding.
- Return calibrated confidence and route only low-confidence or `contradicts` results into the report as `concern`.
- Cost control: run only on citations attached to load-bearing claims, or only when a cheaper check already flagged the document.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every finding cites a verifiable passage from the source, verified programmatically before the finding is emitted
- [ ] Evaluated against a hand-built set of ~20 known-good and known-bad claim/source pairs, with the confusion matrix recorded in this issue
- [ ] Per-document token/cost ceiling enforced
- [ ] Output is framed for a human reviewer to check, never as a final verdict

## Notes

This is the highest-risk check for false positives, and a false accusation of misrepresenting a source is far more costly to the funder than a miss. Bias the thresholds hard toward silence. Ship it behind `--tier llm` and off by default until the eval numbers justify otherwise.

bscriptions"}],"author_association":"OWNER","body":"## Why

Claims are the unit that feeds three other features: similarity across proposals, the achievability read, and the claim-support citation check. Extracting them once and reusing them keeps LLM spend down.

## Scope

- LLM pass that pulls out the load-bearing claims: what will be built//proven, what outcome is promised, what timeline and scale, what is asserted about prior work or the team's track record.
- Each claim carries a `Span`, a type tag (`capability` | `outcome` | `timeline` | `prior-work` | `impact`), and any citation attached to it.
- Structured output (JSON schema / tool use), not prose parsing.
- Flag claims that are quantitative but unsourced — a promised 10x improvement with no citation is exactly what a reviewer wants their eye drawn to.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Structured claims with spans, stable enough to diff between runs on the same document
- [ ] Extraction is idempotent and cached per document hash
- [ ] Manual review on 5 real proposals confirms the claims extracted are the ones a program officer would care about
- [ ] Unsourced quantitative claims are counted in the report summary

## Notes

Resist the temptation to score claims here ("unachievable"), which is a separate judgment needing domain context. This issue is extraction only; the achievability read belongs with budget feasibility.

{"number":16,"title":"Solicitation compliance checks","body":"## Why

The most immediately useful, least controversial feature. Program staff currently do this by hand on every submission, and it's entirely mechanical.

## Scope

- A solicitation spec format (YAML) capturing: required sections, page/word limits, formatting requirements (font, margins, spacing), budget ceiling, eligibility criteria, deadline, required attachments, prohibited content.
- Deterministic checks against the spec: section presence, length limits, budget total vs. ceiling, attachment presence.
- LLM-assisted checks for the judgment-dependent ones (does this address the stated priority area, does the applicant meet stated eligibility), reported as `notice` rather than `fail`.
- Optional: an LLM pass that drafts a spec YAML from a solicitation PDF, for a human to review and correct before use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One YAML spec drives the whole check; adding a new solicitation requires no code
- [ ] Deterministic and judgment-based compliance findings are visually distinct in the report
- [ ] A generated spec is always presented as a draft for human confirmation, never applied silently
- [ ] Works on a real solicitation the team can share, end to end

## Notes

Eligibility determinations have real consequences for applicants, so keep the tool advisory: it flags "page limit is 10, this appears to be 14" for a human to confirm. It never rejects anything. Worth spelling that out in the README too.

{"number":71,"title":"Harness follow-up: post-ingest mutation + real-fixture support","body":"Follow-up to #29 (MVP validation harness). #29 plants defects into fabricated `.md` fixtures **pre-ingest** and scores recall — enough to prove the harness pattern works, but it doesn't exercise the loader in the recall measurement and it doesn't run against any real academic writing. This issue tracks two extensions deferred from that MVP.

## 1. Post-ingest mutation path

Apply defects to `FlattenedDoc.text` *after* the loader runs, so mutations happen on text that has actually been extracted from a real PDF (or DOCX/HTML) fixture. Why it matters:

- The current pre-ingest path can only mutate formats we author by hand (markdown). Anything defect-y in the PDF loader itself (dropped whitespace, mis-ordered columns, footnote handling) is invisible to recall.
- Post-ingest mutation lets us reuse any real document as a substrate: run it through the loader once, capture the `FlattenedDoc`, then plant defects into `.text` and re-run the checkers against the mutated flattened doc.
- The mutation API from #29 (defect specs -> mutator functions) should port over cleanly; the change is *where* in the pipeline the mutation is spliced in.

## 2. Task Exposure paper as a real fixture source

Dan has the Task Exposure paper locally (already used as pat-helper's real fixture; lives in `~/code/pat-helper/data/` as LaTeX). It's a real academic paper, not a grant application, so the `CLAUDE.md` "no real applicant material in the test corpus" rule doesn't apply — this is exactly the kind of real-world writing we want the harness to exercise against.

Two routes to using it, either unblocks this:

- **(a) `.tex` ingest path in slopchecker.** Currently only PDF/DOCX/MD/HTML/TXT are supported. Adding LaTeX would let the paper flow through the pipeline in its native form.
- **(b) Compile `.tex` -> PDF, then use the post-ingest mutation path from item 1.** No new loader needed, but depends on item 1 landing first.

## Dependencies

Blocked on **either** #22 (Alex's synthetic PDF fixture corpus, which gives us real-PDF substrates for the post-ingest path) **or** the `.tex` ingest route above. Not blocked on both — either substrate source unblocks the work.

Natural successor to #29 once the MVP harness lands.

No — there's no issue titled or scoped around "evaluation rubrics" in this repo. I searched all 37 issues (titles, bodies, comments) for `rubric`/`evaluat`/`scoring criteria` and found nothing dedicated to that.

Closest related work:
- **#29** (closed) — *Validation harness: planted-defect fixtures with measured recall* — plants known defects, reruns the pipeline, scores recall with an LLM judge.
- **#71** (open) — *Harness follow-up: post-ingest mutation + real-fixture support* — extends #29 to real PDF fixtures.
- **#11** (open) — *Citation check: does the reference support the claim?* — its acceptance criteria call for evaluating against a hand-built confusion matrix.
- A comment on **#13** (claim extraction) explicitly notes that "run-to-run stability diffing" needs its own scoring harness and was **"deferred to a separate evaluation ticket"** — but that ticket was never actually filed as far as I can find.

So if you're looking to formalize scoring/grading criteria for how well checks perform, that gap in #13's comment thread looks like the natural issue to file. Want me to draft one (referencing #13/#29/#71) rather than continue assuming it exists?

{
  "number": 71,
  "title": "Harness follow-up: post-ingest mutation + real-fixture support",
  "body": "Follow-up to #29 (MVP validation harness). #29 plants defects into fabricated `.md` fixtures **pre-ingest** and scores recall — enough to prove the harness pattern works, but it doesn't exercise the loader in the recall measurement and it doesn't run against any real academic writing. This issue tracks two extensions deferred from that MVP.

## 1. Post-ingest mutation path

Apply defects to `FlattenedDoc.text` *after* the loader runs, so mutations happen on text that has actually been extracted from a real PDF (or DOCX/HTML) fixture. Why it matters:

- The current pre-ingest path can only mutate formats we author by hand (markdown). Anything defect-y in the PDF loader itself (dropped whitespace, mis-ordered columns, footnote handling) is invisible to recall.
- Post-ingest mutation lets us reuse any real document as a substrate: run it through the loader once, capture the `FlattenedDoc`, then plant defects into `.text` and re-run the checkers against the mutated flattened doc.
- The mutation API from #29 (defect specs -> mutator functions) should port over cleanly; the change is *where* in the pipeline the mutation is spliced in.

## 2. Task Exposure paper as a real fixture source

Dan has the Task Exposure paper locally (already used as pat-helper's real fixture; lives in `~/code/pat-helper/data/` as LaTeX). It's a real academic paper, not a grant application, so the `CLAUDE.md` "no real applicant material in the test corpus" rule doesn't apply — this is exactly the kind of real-world writing we want the harness to exercise against.

Two routes to using it, either unblocks this:

- **(a) `.tex` ingest path in slopchecker.** Currently only PDF/DOCX/MD/HTML/TXT are supported. Adding LaTeX would let the paper flow through the pipeline in its native form.
- **(b) Compile `.tex` -> PDF, then use the post-in

{
  "number": 13,
  "title": "Extract core claims from a submission",
  "body": "## Why

Claims are the unit that feeds three other features: similarity across proposals, the achievability read, and the claim-support citation check. Extracting them once and reusing them keeps LLM spend down.

## Scope

- LLM pass that pulls out the load-bearing claims: what will be built//proven, what outcome is promised, what timeline and scale, what is asserted about prior work or the team's track record.
- Each claim carries a `Span`, a type tag (`capability` | `outcome` | `timeline` | `prior-work` | `impact`), and any citation attached to it.
- Structured output (JSON schema / tool use), not prose parsing.
- Flag claims that are quantitative but unsourced — a promised 10x improvement with no citation is exactly what a reviewer wants their eye drawn to.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Structured claims with spans, stable enough to diff between runs on the same document
- [ ] Extraction is idempotent and cached per document hash
- [ ] Manual review on 5 real proposals confirms the claims extracted are the ones a program officer would care about
- [ ] Unsourced quantitative claims are counted in the report summary

## Notes

Resist the temptation to score claims here ("unachievable"), which is a separate judgment needing domain context. This issue is extraction only; the achievability read belongs with budget feasibility.

{
  "number": 11,
  "title": "Citation check: does the reference actually support the claim it's cited for?",
  "body": "## Why

The deepest version of citation checking, and the one that catches sophisticated slop: real paper, correct metadata, real quote — cited for a claim it does not support.

## Scope

- For each (claim sentence, citation) pair with retrievable source text, ask an LLM whether the source supports, partially supports, is unrelated to, or contradicts the claim.
- Ground the judgment: require the model to return the supporting passage from the source, and drop any verdict whose quoted passage isn't actually in the retrieved text. No passage, no finding.
- Return calibrated confidence and route only low-confidence or `contradicts` results into the report as `concern`.
- Cost control: run only on citations attached to load-bearing claims, or only when a cheaper check already flagged the document.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every finding cites a verifiable passage from the source, verified programmatically before the finding is emitted
- [ ] Evaluated against a hand-built set of ~20 known-good and known-bad claim/source pairs, with the confusion matrix recorded in this issue
- [ ] Per-document token/cost ceiling enforced
- [ ] Output is framed for a human reviewer to check, never as a final verdict

## Notes

This is the highest-risk check for false positives, and a false accusation of misrepresenting a source is far more costly to the funder than a miss. Bias the thresholds hard toward silence. Ship it behind `--tier llm` and off by default until the eval numbers justify otherwise.
",

{"number":81,"title":"Integration tests: full CLI chain (run → report.json/HTML → render --pdf) on fabricated fixtures","body":"Turn the 2026-07-31 manual e2e smoke (see `ai-log/2026-07-31-danparshall-pdf-macos-hang.md`, PR #78) into repeatable integration tests. The full chain is verified by hand but has no committed test:

```
fabricated .pdf → slopcheck run  --format json,html → report.json + report.html
report.json → slopcheck render  --pdf → paginated PDF
```

## Scope

- `tests/test_integration_e2e.py` behind a `@pytest.mark.integration` marker (register in `pyproject.toml`; default unit run stays fast). Drive the real CLI via `typer.testing.CliRunner` or `subprocess`.
- Cases:
  - PDF → `run` → `report.json` validates against `EvidenceReport` (`src/slopchecker/models.py`, `docs/DATA_MODEL.md`) + HTML written.
  - `render --pdf`: assert `%PDF-` magic + nonzero size. Gate on `find_browser() is not None`, but **fail loudly where a browser is expected** (macOS dev machines, CI) — the "2 skipped forever" trap is exactly what hid the bug #78 fixed.
  - Degrade-to-gaps, never crash: scanned/no-text-layer PDF → gap row not stack trace; unsupported suffix; corrupt PDF. Patterns in `tests/test_cli_run.py` and `tests/test_ingest.py` (`make_pdf` helper).
  - Batch mode: folder of mixed fixtures → per-file reports + gap rows for the duds.
- Fixtures: fabricated only (house rule). Reuse #22 fixtures and the #79 harness corpus where they fit.

## Non-scope

- **Not** recall scoring — that's the #29 planted-defect harness, landed as #79. This issue is CI-grade chain plumbing: does the pipeline hold together, does every leg produce its artifact, do failures degrade to gaps.
- No changes inside `src/slopchecker/report/` (Emerson) or `src/slopchecker/checks/` (Nick) — tests exercise them, don't edit them.

## Practicalities

- `uv sync --all-extras` (plain `uv sync` installs no pytest).
- CI is a required check on ubuntu; chromium is present but see #47/#49/#51 history before touching anything browser-adjacent in CI config.
- Branch `/-integration-tests`; STATUS.md line + ai-log entry ride the PR.

Origin: Dan + Fable e2e smoke session, 2026-07-31 (which also produced #78).

slopcheck config

It failed on `scripts/transcript_prompt.py` and `scripts/upload_transcript.py`, which predate the formatter config — didn't want to put a whitespace diff on @990991A / @etbrooking's files without a heads-up. LLM fallback out of scope for this PR.","html_url":"https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/issues/7#issuecomment-5145000873","user":{"login":"danparshall","id":8367780,"profile_url":"https://github.com/danparshall","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/8367780?v=4"},"author_association":"COLLABORATOR","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-31T16:12:29Z","updated_at":"2026-07-31T16:12:29Z"},{"id":5145171440,"body":"Landed in #59 (CI green) — Dan (+ Fable session).

**What shipped:** `src/slopchecker/pipeline/citations/` — `extract_citations(text, ref_region=None) -> CitationExtraction`. Reference parsing for APA / Chicago author-date / numbered-IEEE (authors, year+suffix, title, venue, DOI, URL, arXiv ID, pages); in-text markers (parenthetical incl. multi-cite and `p. 14`, narrative, numeric `[3, 4]`); claim sentence + `Span` per mention (ready for #11); marker↔entry linking; unlinked markers emitted as quote-anchored `Finding`s with `citation_has_reference: false`. Types live in the pipeline package — `models.py` untouched; will propose promotion on #3 if other checkers want them.

**P/R against the hand-labeled fixture corpus** (three fabricated docs, one per style, `tests/fixtures/citations/`):

| metric | P | R | gold n |
|---|---|---|---|
| mention detection | 1.00 | 1.00 | 21 |
| reference entries | 1.00 | 1.00 | 12 |
| mention→ref links (incl. planted unlinked defects) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 22 |

Caveat, stated plainly: the corpus is small and clean. These numbers validate the happy paths of all three styles plus the planted defects; real flattened-PDF text will be uglier and the parser will need iteration against it.

**Explicitly out of scope this PR:** footnote-style superscript markers (don't survive text flattening reliably), `[1]-[3]` range expansion (parsed as two cites, middle not expanded), LLM fallback for entries the regex can't parse, registry (#5) wiring.

[{"id":5145656059,"body":"**Claimed — Nick (claude-code). Implemented; PR #80 open.** Don't start a parallel lane on this one.

Branch `claude/checks-deterministic-tier-xc57l0`, rebased on current main (post-#15, post-#58). Three checks land against this issue, in `src/slopchecker/checks/`:

- `citation_identifiers_valid` — offline: DOI pattern, ISBN-10/13 checksums, arXiv ids (incl. impossible-month rejection), URL parseability
- `all_dois_resolve` — **via doi.org, not the Crossref API**, so DataCite/mEDRA DOIs count; querying Crossref alone would have read a real DataCite DOI as fabricated
- `all_urls_resolve` — plain reference URLs, kept as a separate row so ordinary link rot in gray literature doesn't inflate the DOI headline number

### Design decisions, for the record

**Four outcomes, and only one of them counts against a document.** `resolves / not_found / blocked / unreachable`. Only 404/410 flips a ledger row false. Paywalls, bot walls and rate limits (401/403/429/451) and 5xx/timeouts become *per-item coverage gaps* — a `CheckResult` with `status="skipped"` and a reason, which Emerson's renderer already draws as a gray chip. We didn't learn the source is missing; we learned we couldn't look. This is the issue's "be conservative in wording" note made structural rather than aspirational.

**Transport failures are tracked separately from HTTP answers**, which is how the second AC is satisfied: a run where nothing answered at all reports `errored` with "network failure, not a citation defect", instead of quietly reporting that every citation is dead.

**Malformed ≠ unresolvable.** The offline check owns typos and the network checks skip malformed identifiers entirely, so one defect never shows up twice under two names.

**Cache** is keyed on the identifier (not the document), so a DOI cited by forty proposals in a batch is fetched once. `--only all_dois_resolve` over the fixture is 3.6s cold / 0.4s warm. Escape hatch is `slopcheck run --no-cache`, plus `--cache-dir`; corrupt or unwritable cache degrades to a miss. Transport errors are deliberately never cached — caching "the network was down" would poison later runs.

**Tier is `deterministic`, not `api`**, per CLAUDE.md's ownership table: no key, no LLM, `needs_network=True` is what gates them. `CROSSREF_MAILTO` is used for the polite-pool User-Agent only and nothing is gated on it, per the warning in `config.py`.

### Cross-module edits (small, additive — shout if you'd rather they didn't)

- `pipeline/registry.py`: two optional `CheckContext` fields, `no_cache` and `cache_dir`. Defaults preserve behavior.
- `cli.py`: `--no-cache` / `--cache-dir` on `slopcheck run`, since this issue's AC requires the escape hatch.

### One risk to flag

`tests/test_checks_live.py` hits doi.org/Crossref/OpenAlex/arXiv for real (deliberate call). CI is a required check on main, so a provider hiccup can redden the build for everyone. Every decision the module makes on its own is covered offline, so the fix if it becomes routine is a marker gating that file behind `SLOPCHECK_LIVE=1` — noted at the top of the file. The upside already paid off once: it caught that arXiv 503s constantly and our arXiv provider was the one path missing the retry ladder.

[{"id":5145660056,"body":"**Claimed — Nick (claude-code). Implemented; PR #80 open** (same PR as #8 — #9 reuses #8's HTTP client and cache, so splitting them would have meant writing the fetch layer twice). Don't start a parallel lane.

`metadata_match` in `src/slopchecker/checks/metadata_match.py`, with `providers.py` (Crossref → OpenAlex → arXiv behind one `MetadataProvider` interface) and `compare.py` (fuzzy grading).

### Design decisions, for the record

**Title decides, author and year escalate a doubt, venue never decides alone.** Venue disagreement is constant on honest citations — abbreviations, imprints, preprint servers — so letting it vote would have produced a fabrication signal out of ordinary sloppiness. Abbreviated venues, initials instead of given names, dropped subtitles and ±1 year for online-first all grade `minor` and don't flip the ledger row. `different` is reserved for the failure this issue is actually about: a real identifier on a reference describing another paper.

**A missing canonical record is our coverage gap, not the applicant's defect.** Books and gray literature — think tank reports especially, i.e. much of what our users cite — aren't in any of the three providers. Those report "not covered by our metadata providers" and are *excluded from the match tally* rather than counted against anyone. Expect and report low confidence there rather than crying fabrication, as the issue asks.

**Reverse lookup is implemented and is the thing I'd demo.** When an identifier has no record we search by title+author anyway; a hit at ≥0.80 title similarity reports *"no record for this DOI, but a work with this title exists (DOI 10.x/y) — the identifier looks wrong."* That's a wrong citation, not an invented one, and it flips the ledger row while saying so in those words.

**Thresholds live in module constants** (`TITLE_STRONG=0.90`, `TITLE_WEAK=0.70`, `YEAR_TOLERANCE=1`, …) so they're tunable against fixtures without touching check code. `tests/test_checks_compare.py` is the tuning record — the load-bearing cases there are the negative ones.

### Two calibration bugs worth knowing about (both fixed, both have regression tests)

1. **Token-overlap similarity divided by `min()`**, so any title whose words were a *subset* of the canonical's scored a perfect 1.0. "Thermometry of a living cell **nucleus**" matched the paper it merely extends. Now Jaccard; truncated subtitles are handled explicitly instead, where the truncation is the point.
2. **Don't split the cited author on a comma.** IEEE style is "G. Kucsko", so that yielded a surname of *"G. Kucsko"* and graded every correctly-cited IEEE reference in the fixture as a minor discrepancy against its own source. `citations.first_surname` (#7) already handles both author shapes — use it.

Both were caught by the fixture's *honest* reference, which is why there's now an explicit "the correctly cited reference produces no finding" test. A false-positive guard is worth more here than another true-positive case.

### Coverage

Live tests confirm the real behavior end to end: Crossref and OpenAlex both answer for the same DOI with the same normalized shape, the reverse lookup finds the real DOI from the title alone, and a fabricated title returns nothing (no false "found it elsewhere"). ISBNs are checksum-validated but not *resolved* — no book provider wired up; noted as remaining work.

[{"id":5143877199,"body":"Adjacent to this: pushed `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root (28e3784) — conventions for everyone's Claude/AI sessions. Issue-first workflow, the design decisions already locked (binary check results, `report.json` as the contract, mockups as HTML), and a "show your work" rule: session logs in `ai-log/` plus automatic transcript upload to `ai-log/transcripts/` via a checked-in project hook (`.claude/settings.json` → `scripts/upload_transcript.py`), per Nick's real-time suggestion.

Heads-up for the team: the hook fires when you next run Claude Code in this repo (it'll ask you to trust project settings). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy the current Claude Code session transcript into ai-log/transcripts/.

Wired up as a project hook in .claude/settings.json:
  Stop       -> copy transcript into the working tree
  SessionEnd -> copy + git add/commit/push (--push)

Best-effort by design: always exits 0 so a logging failure never blocks a
session. OPT-IN: does nothing unless enabled via SLOPCHECK_TRANSCRIPT=1 in
your environment, or a .slopcheck-transcript file (gitignored, content "1")
at the repo root — written by the session after asking you, see
transcript_prompt.py. Personal context injected by your own hooks/memory
would otherwise end up in a public repo.

The repo is public. Obvious credential patterns are scrubbed before the copy,
but scrubbing is best-effort — don't paste secrets into sessions here.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

REDACTIONS = [
    re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}"),
    re.compile(r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"),
    re.compile(r"github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}"),
    re.compile(r"gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"),
    re.compile(r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"),
    re.compile(r"xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9\-]{10,}"),
    re.compile(r"Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-._~+/]{20,}"),
    re.compile(r"(?i)(api[_-]?key|secret|password|token)([\"'\\\s]*[:=][\"'\\\s]*)[A-Za-z0-9\-._]{16,}"),
]


def scrub(text: str) -> str:
    for pat in REDACTIONS:
        if pat.groups:
            text = pat.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + m.group(2) + "[REDACTED]", text)
        else:
            text = pat.sub("[REDACTED]", text)
    return text


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60
    )
    return out.stdout.strip()


def enabled(root: Path) -> bool:
    env = os.environ.get("SLOPCHECK_TRANSCRIPT")
    if env in ("0", "1"):
        return env == "1"
    pref = root / ".slopcheck-transcript"
    return pref.is_file() and pref.read_text().strip() == "1"


def main() -> None:

    payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    src = Path(payload.get("transcript_path", ""))
    if not src.is_file():
        return

    root = Path(git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel") or ".")
    if not enabled(root):
        return
    dest_dir = root / "ai-log" / "transcripts"
    dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    user = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_\-]", "", git("config", "user.name") or "unknown") or "unknown"
    session8 = (payload.get("session_id") or "nosession")[:8]
    dest = dest_dir / f"{date.today().isoformat()}-{user}-{session8}.jsonl"

    dest.write_text(scrub(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")), encoding="utf-8")

    if "--push" in sys.argv:
        rel = dest.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        git("add", rel)
        git("commit", "-m", f"transcript: {user} {session8}", "--", rel)
        git("pull", "--rebase", "origin", "main")
        git("push", "origin", "main")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception:
        pass  # logging must never block a session
    sys.exit(0)

# Proposal Slopchecker team doc

  

Teammates

  - Nick Wagner - Learning Journey AI Inc
  - Dan Parshall - 
  - Emerson - Atlantic Council Research Lab
  - Alex - Bipartisan Policy Center
  - Dominique Ramsawak (joining soon)

  

Github link: <https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker/>

  

# Problem: 

Too many slop submissions coming into funding orgs. We want to make an open source utility to automate some of the basic checks needed to identify AI-generated content, check solicitation compliance, and perform basic proposal tagging.

  - Pitching things that are unachievable 
  - Reputational harm in publishing or giving platform to something AI-generated

  

Resources:

  - IFP’s own tool for this: <https://github.com/JayIoAurelius/tls-review-shared> 
  - Candid grants dataset: https://data.candid.org/reference/grants-datasets

  

Feature list:

  - Open source
  - Pangram checks through API
  - Citation checker - even if legit, first order source review
      
      - Is citation validly formatted? (e.g. does DOI resolve) 
      - Does the source match what is being cited (e.g. is name matching what is in the paper)
      - If a quote, is the quote existing in the paper
      - Does the reference actually match the claim being made in the citing paper
  - Extract core claims from submission
  - Compute similarity to existing submitted proposals
      
      - And reviewer pool if available
  - Tag document with topics, submitter type
  - Auto generate deep research reports on submitting team and topic
  - Check compliance with solicitation (if relevant)
  - Is budget feasible (if relevant)
  - Types of documents to support: 
      
      - Grant applications
      - Blog posts
      - Think tank reports 

  

What might output look like:

  - Evidence report (\# of DOI’s that don’t resolve, detection scores) 
  - Deterministic checks (DOI resolution, metadata, solicitation compliance)
  - More complex/expensive: Pangram, 
  - In-line annotation of above  (HTML)

Your email (`monsieurwagner@gmail.com`) lines up with Nick Wagner / `nawagner`, the repo owner, so you're squarely on the team.

**#24 is open to take:**
- No assignee, no "claiming" comment from anyone — genuinely unclaimed.
- Labeled `good first issue`, P0.
- Not tied to a named module owner in CLAUDE.md's ownership table (README/CONTRIBUTING isn't `pipeline/`, `checks/`, `report/`, etc.), so there's no one to coordinate with before starting.
- Dan already left a scoping comment on it noting everything needed to document has landed (data model, CLI tiers, ingest, lens format) — so it's ready to write, not blocked on other work.

(For the record on #20 you asked about first: also genuinely unclaimed, P1, but it's tagged `area:reporting` which per the ownership table is Emerson's/Dominique's territory — worth a heads-up comment on the issue before diving in, unlike #24.)

Want me to go ahead and post a "claiming" comment on #24, then start a new branch (`nick/24-readme-contributing` per the repo's naming convention) to write the README/CONTRIBUTING?

content.text:
Two things going on here, and I want to flag a real conflict before acting.

**The conflict:** Your personal stop-hook wants commits identified as `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` (with the harness's signing key) so GitHub shows "Verified." But this repo's `CLAUDE.md` has an explicit, deliberate policy that overrides defaults: use a real name/email (e.g. `"Nick (claude-code)"` + your real address) so GitHub attributes commits to the actual person, with a `Co-Authored-By` trailer for the model. Those two are mutually exclusive for the same commit — and I found the harness's SSH-signing setup only produces a valid signature for the generic `Claude` identity anyway (I checked: my commits came out unsigned even with `commit.gpgsign=true` set, because they were made as direct `git commit` calls, not through whatever wrapper actually invokes the signer).

I'm going to follow CLAUDE.md (the project's explicit, checked-in instruction) rather than the generic personal hook — an "Unverified" badge is a cosmetic GitHub label, it doesn't block merges, and misattributing commits away from the real contributor is the worse failure mode here. Let me know if you'd rather I do the opposite for this repo.

I also found the messy cause: the `SessionEnd` hook auto-ran `upload_transcript.py --push`, which (per its known bug, tracked in #30) does `git pull --rebase origin main` on whatever branch is checked out — it rebased our feature branch onto main and left two duplicate "transcript" commits with the wrong (generic) identity. Cleaning that into one properly-attributed commit now, then moving to #24.

[project]
name = "slopchecker"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Automating slop checks for funding proposals"
requires-python = ">=3.11"

dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.7",
    "typer>=0.12",
    "rich>=13.7",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Heavy/optional deps live behind extras so someone working on citations
# doesn't need the PDF or LLM stack installed (see #2).
pdf = ["pymupdf>=1.24"]
docx = ["python-docx>=1.1"]
llm = ["anthropic>=0.40"]
# The web layer over the pipeline (#27) — see slopchecker/web.py.
web = ["fastapi>=0.115", "uvicorn>=0.30", "python-multipart>=0.0.9"]
# Validation harness (#29): planted-defect injector + recall report.
harness = ["pyyaml>=6.0"]
dev = ["ruff>=0.5", "pytest>=8.2", "mypy>=1.10"]

[project.scripts]
slopcheck = "slopchecker.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/slopchecker"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Default run = fast unit suite. Integration (full CLI chain, #81) is opt-in:
# `pytest -m integration`. CI runs both as separate steps.
addopts = "-m 'not integration'"
markers = [
    "integration: full CLI chain in real subprocesses (opt in: pytest -m integration)",
]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
packages = ["slopchecker"]
# Non-blocking to start (#2) — tighten once the data model in #3 lands.
ignore_missing_imports = true

1	# DATA_MODEL.md — the report.json contract (#3)
2	
3	`report.json` is the contract between checkers and the renderer. It is
4	defined once, as pydantic models, in `src/slopchecker/models.py`. This doc
5	is the human-readable mirror; if they disagree, the code wins — and please
6	open an issue comment on #3.
7	
8	Naming: CLAUDE.md's names won over the issue-#3 strawman —
9	**`FlattenedDoc` / `Finding` / `EvidenceReport`** (aliases `Document` and
10	`Report` exist for code written against the issue text). The field layout
11	codifies the shape already shipped by the renderer (#35/#40); the reference
12	instance is `tests/fixtures/sample_report.json`, and
13	`EvidenceReport.to_report_dict()` emits exactly what
14	`report.html.render_report()` consumes.
15	
16	Ground rules baked into the types:
17	
18	- **Check results are `true | false | number` — never free text.** Strings
19	  are rejected at validation time, even `"true"`. Human framing lives in
20	  the renderer.
21	- **Findings are evidence, not verdicts.** No `is_ai_generated`-style
22	  fields. A detector score is a number in its own lane; the tool
23	  recommends `human_review`, it never auto-rejects.
24	- **A check that didn't run is first-class.** `status: skipped | errored`
25	  with a mandatory `reason` — never a silently missing result. This is how
26	  "degrade to gaps, never crash" shows up in the data.
27	- **Unknown fields are rejected** (`extra="forbid"`). A typo in a checker's
28	  output fails loudly instead of being silently dropped.
29	
30	## Models
31	
32	### `EvidenceReport` (alias `Report`) — the top level
33	
34	| Field | Type | Meaning |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| `schema_version` | `str` (default `"0.1"`) | Contract version; bump on breaking change |
37	| `document` | `FlattenedDoc` | The normalized document under review |
38	| `solicitation` | `str?` | Solicitation ID the proposal responds to |
39	| `run` | `RunInfo` | When/how long/which code/what cost |
40	| `findings` | `list[Finding]` | Quote-anchored evidence cards |

# DATA_MODEL.md — the report.json contract (#3)

`report.json` is the contract between checkers and the renderer. It is
defined once, as pydantic models, in `src/slopchecker/models.py`. This doc
is the human-readable mirror; if they disagree, the code wins — and please
open an issue comment on #3.

Naming: CLAUDE.md's names won over the issue-#3 strawman —
**`FlattenedDoc` / `Finding` / `EvidenceReport`** (aliases `Document` and
`Report` exist for code written against the issue text). The field layout
codifies the shape already shipped by the renderer (#35/#40); the reference
instance is `tests/fixtures/sample_report.json`, and
`EvidenceReport.to_report_dict()` emits exactly what
`report.html.render_report()` consumes.

Ground rules baked into the types:

- **Check results are `true | false | number` — never free text.** Strings
  are rejected at validation time, even `"true"`. Human framing lives in
  the renderer.
- **Findings are evidence, not verdicts.** No `is_ai_generated`-style
  fields. A detector score is a number in its own lane; the tool
  recommends `human_review`, it never auto-rejects.
- **A check that didn't run is first-class.** `status: skipped | errored`
  with a mandatory `reason` — never a silently missing result. This is how
  "degrade to gaps, never crash" shows up in the data.
- **Unknown fields are rejected** (`extra="forbid"`). A typo in a checker's
  output fails loudly instead of being silently dropped.

## Models

### `EvidenceReport` (alias `Report`) — the top level

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `str` (default `"0.1"`) | Contract version; bump on breaking change |
| `document` | `FlattenedDoc` | The normalized document under review |
| `solicitation` | `str?` | Solicitation ID the proposal responds to |
| `run` | `RunInfo` | When/how long/which code/what cost |
| `findings` | `list[Finding]` | Quote-anchored evidence cards |
| `ledger` | `list[LedgerRow]` | Document-level all-checks table |
| `summary` | `Summary` | Recommendation (always advisory) |

Methods: `counts()` derives `passed/failed/scores/skipped/errored` tallies
from the ledger (never stored — Emerson's rule on #3). `to_report_dict()`
returns the JSON-ready dict the renderer takes.

### `FlattenedDoc` (alias `Document`)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | `str` | Source filename |
| `text` | `str` | The single normalized text all anchors index into |
| `sha256` | `str?` | Hash of the source file |
| `pages` | `int?` | Page count |
| `page_offsets` | `list[int]?` | Char offset in `text` where each page starts (#4) |
| `media_type` | `str?` | Source type, e.g. `application/pdf` |
| `title`, `byline`, `submitter` | `str?` | Display metadata |

Section structure is deferred until a loader needs it.

### `Finding`

One quote-anchored piece of evidence. Rendered as an annotation card
beside the passage it refers to.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `str` | Short card ID (`C3`, `Q1`, `D1`) |
| `target` | `str?` | What it's about (`ref[3]`, `p2`) |
| `label` | `str?` | Card title; renderer falls back to `target`/`id` |
| `anchor` | `Anchor?` | Where in the document this points |
| `checks` | `list[CheckResult]` | The bool/number results |
| `verdict` | `Verdict?` | Closed enum for LLM claim-support judgments (#11) |
| `evidence` | `dict` | Raw supporting data — enough for a human to verify without re-running (resolved metadata, HTTP status, source excerpt, model + score details) |
| `note` | `str?` | One line max. Enforced. |

`Verdict` is `supported | overstated | unsupported | contradicted |
unverifiable`. `overstated` (source supports less than claimed) is
deliberately distinct from `unsupported` (no support) and `contradicted`
(source refutes); `unverifiable` (paywalled / not retrievable) never hides
inside `unsupported`.

### `Anchor` and `Span`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Anchor.page` | `int?` (≥1) | Page the quote appears on |
| `Anchor.quote` | `str` | Verbatim excerpt from `document.text`; must be mechanically grounded (quotecheck) before it reaches the report |
| `Anchor.span` | `Span?` | Exact offsets, when the producer knows them |
| `Span.start`, `Span.end` | `int` (≥0) | Half-open char offsets `[start, end)` into `document.text`; `end ≥ start` enforced |

### `CheckResult` (inside `Finding.checks`)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | Check name (`doi_resolves`, `pangram_span`) |
| `result` | `bool \| int \| float \| null` | The outcome. Strict — strings rejected |
| `status` | `"ok" \| "skipped" \| "errored"` | Whether the check actually ran |
| `reason` | `str?` | Required when status ≠ `ok` |

Consistency is enforced: `ok` requires a `result`; `skipped`/`errored`
require a `reason` and may not carry a `result`.

### `LedgerRow` (inside `EvidenceReport.ledger`)

Same status discipline as `CheckResult`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | `str` | Check name |
| `label` | `str?` | Human label for the table row |
| `result` | `bool \| int \| float \| null` | Outcome |
| `detail` | `str?` | Short context (`"3 / 4 — ref [3] not found"`) |
| `status` / `reason` | as above | First-class skipped/errored |

### `Check` — a check *definition*, not a result

Registry entry so the orchestrator can budget and gate.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `str` | Stable ID, matches `CheckResult.name` / `LedgerRow.check` |
| `name` | `str` | Human name |
| `tier` | `"deterministic" \| "api" \| "llm"` | The deterministic tier must run with no LLM at all |
| `est_cost_usd` | `float` (default 0) | Estimated cost per run |
| `needs_network` | `bool` (default false) | Skip offline |

### `RunInfo` and `Summary`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `RunInfo.date` | `str?` | Run date |
| `RunInfo.seconds` | `int \| float?` | Wall-clock duration |
| `RunInfo.version` | `str?` | slopchecker version that produced the report |
| `RunInfo.cost_usd` | `float?` | Actual spend |
| `Summary.recommendation` | `str` (default `"human_review"`) | Always advisory |

## Worked minimal example

A report with one finding (a citation whose DOI does not resolve), one
score row, and one check that could not run:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "document": {
    "file": "proposal.pdf",
    "text": "Prebunking achieves durable inoculation [1].\n\n[1] Doe, J. (2025). doi:10.1/fabricated"
  },
  "run": { "date": "2026-07-31", "seconds": 12 },
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "C1",
      "target": "ref[1]",
      "label": "Citation [1]",
      "anchor": { "page": 1, "quote": "Prebunking achieves durable inoculation" },
      "checks": [
        { "name": "doi_resolves", "result": false, "status": "ok" }
      ],
      "evidence": { "doi": "10.1/fabricated", "http_status": 404 },
      "note": "DOI does not resolve."
    }
  ],
  "ledger": [
    { "check": "all_dois_resolve", "label": "All DOIs resolve", "result": false, "detail": "0 / 1", "status": "ok" },
    { "check": "pangram_document", "label": "AI detection (Pangram)", "result": 0.96, "detail": "document score", "status": "ok" },
    { "check": "claim_support", "label": "Claims supported by sources", "status": "skipped", "reason": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set" }
  ],
  "summary": { "recommendation": "human_review" }
}
```

Render it: `slopcheck render report.json` (add `--pdf` for the shipping
artifact). Producing one from models:

```python
from slopchecker.models import EvidenceReport, FlattenedDoc

report = EvidenceReport(document=FlattenedDoc(file="proposal.pdf", text="..."))
report_json = report.model_dump_json(exclude_none=True)      # to disk
report = EvidenceReport.model_validate_json(report_json)     # from disk
html_input = report.to_report_dict()                         # for report/html.py
```

## Running the tests

From the repo root (after `uv venv` + `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`; add
`,web,pdf` extras to cover the web stub and PDF loaders):

```bash
uv run pytest                        # everything
uv run pytest tests/test_models.py   # just the data model
uv run pytest tests/test_models.py -k round_trip   # one shape of test
uv run ruff check .                  # lint (CI runs this too)
```

Which tests cover which modules:

| Test file | Covers |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_models.py` | `src/slopchecker/models.py` (this contract), incl. one wiring test through `report/html.py` |
| `tests/test_config.py` | `src/slopchecker/config.py` |
| `tests/test_web.py` | `src/slopchecker/web.py` |
| `tests/test_report_html.py` | `src/slopchecker/report/html.py` |
| `tests/test_report_pdf.py` | `src/slopchecker/report/pdf.py` (skips without a Chromium-family browser) |

House rule (CLAUDE.md): **agents run the tests they touched before opening
a PR.** If you change `models.py`, that means at minimum
`uv run pytest tests/test_models.py tests/test_report_html.py` — the
renderer consumes what these models emit. And changing a shared model =
comment on #3 first.

1	# Lens prompt packs
2	
3	A **lens** is one LLM pass over a submission, defined entirely in a
4	markdown file in this directory. Prompts are data, not code: teammates
5	add or edit lenses without touching Python, and every lens gets format
6	validation from the shared tests for free.
7	
8	The Python here (`loader.py`) only parses markdown into a `Lens` object.
9	Prompt assembly, the LLM client, retries, and per-document caching are
10	the pipeline engine's job (#37) — nothing in this directory calls a
11	model.
12	
13	## File format
14	
15	One lens per file, `<lens-id>.md`:
16	
17	```markdown
18	---
19	id: my-lens          # must match the filename stem
20	issue: 42            # tracking issue number
21	version: 0.1
22	output: json
23	---
24	
25	# Human-readable lens title
26	
27	## Purpose
28	
29	One paragraph: what this lens extracts/judges and who consumes it.
30	
31	## System prompt
32	
33	The full system prompt sent to the model. Hard constraints go here,
34	numbered.
35	
36	## Output format
37	
38	The JSON shape the model must emit, in a ```json fence, plus how the
39	pipeline maps it onto the shared `Finding` model (#3).
40	
41	## Example
42	
43	### Input
44	
45	One fenced block: a fabricated document excerpt, with `[[page N]]`
46	markers.
47	
48	### Output
49	
50	One fenced block: the exact JSON the model should produce for that
51	input.
52	```
53	
54	Frontmatter is flat `key: value` lines only. `System prompt`,
55	`Output format`, and `Example` (with Input/Output fences) are required —
56	the loader refuses files without them. Extra sections are fine and are
57	preserved.
58	
59	## Rules every lens must honor
60	
61	These come from the repo-wide design decisions in `CLAUDE.md`:
62	
63	- **Quote-anchored.** Any `quote` the model emits must be a verbatim,
64	  contiguous substring of the input. `tests/test_lenses.py` checks this
65	  mechanically for every lens's example — if your few-shot paraphrases,
66	  the suite fails.
67	- **No free text in the evidence layer.** Model output is structured
68	  JSON; check results downstream are strictly `bool | float`. Reader
69	  prose belongs to the renderer.
70	- **Evidence, not verdicts.** A lens extracts or measures; it does not
71	  recommend rejection.
72	- **Fabricated examples only.** Few-shot inputs are invented documents —
73	  never real applicant material.
74	
75	## Adding a lens
76	
77	1. Copy the skeleton above into `<lens-id>.md`.
78	2. Write the few-shot with a fabricated input; make sure every quote in
79	   the Output is copy-pasted from the Input.
80	3. Run `pytest tests/test_lenses.py` — the generic tests pick up the new
81	   file automatically.
82	4. Open an issue comment describing the lens's output contract if it
83	   introduces new check names (see #3 before extending the `Finding`
84	   shape).
85	
86	## Using a lens
87	
88	```python
89	from slopchecker.lenses import list_lenses, load_lens
90	
91	lens = load_lens("claims")
92	lens.meta  # frontmatter dict
93	lens.system_prompt  # section text
94	lens.output_format
95	lens.example_input  # fenced block contents
96	lens.example_output
97	```

# Lens prompt packs

A **lens** is one LLM pass over a submission, defined entirely in a
markdown file in this directory. Prompts are data, not code: teammates
add or edit lenses without touching Python, and every lens gets format
validation from the shared tests for free.

The Python here (`loader.py`) only parses markdown into a `Lens` object.
Prompt assembly, the LLM client, retries, and per-document caching are
the pipeline engine's job (#37) — nothing in this directory calls a
model.

## File format

One lens per file, `<lens-id>.md`:

```markdown
---
id: my-lens          # must match the filename stem
issue: 42            # tracking issue number
version: 0.1
output: json
---

# Human-readable lens title

## Purpose

One paragraph: what this lens extracts/judges and who consumes it.

## System prompt

The full system prompt sent to the model. Hard constraints go here,
numbered.

## Output format

The JSON shape the model must emit, in a ```json fence, plus how the
pipeline maps it onto the shared `Finding` model (#3).

## Example

### Input

One fenced block: a fabricated document excerpt, with `[[page N]]`
markers.

### Output

One fenced block: the exact JSON the model should produce for that
input.
```

Frontmatter is flat `key: value` lines only. `System prompt`,
`Output format`, and `Example` (with Input/Output fences) are required —
the loader refuses files without them. Extra sections are fine and are
preserved.

## Rules every lens must honor

These come from the repo-wide design decisions in `CLAUDE.md`:

- **Quote-anchored.** Any `quote` the model emits must be a verbatim,
  contiguous substring of the input. `tests/test_lenses.py` checks this
  mechanically for every lens's example — if your few-shot paraphrases,
  the suite fails.
- **No free text in the evidence layer.** Model output is structured
  JSON; check results downstream are strictly `bool | float`. Reader
  prose belongs to the renderer.
- **Evidence, not verdicts.** A lens extracts or measures; it does not
  recommend rejection.
- **Fabricated examples only.** Few-shot inputs are invented documents —
  never real applicant material.

## Adding a lens

1. Copy the skeleton above into `<lens-id>.md`.
2. Write the few-shot with a fabricated input; make sure every quote in
   the Output is copy-pasted from the Input.
3. Run `pytest tests/test_lenses.py` — the generic tests pick up the new
   file automatically.
4. Open an issue comment describing the lens's output contract if it
   introduces new check names (see #3 before extending the `Finding`
   shape).

## Using a lens

```python
from slopchecker.lenses import list_lenses, load_lens

lens = load_lens("claims")
lens.meta  # frontmatter dict
lens.system_prompt  # section text
lens.output_format
lens.example_input  # fenced block contents
lens.example_output
```

1	"""Built-in trivial checks (#5): the registry's proof of life.
2	
3	These exist so a fresh checkout produces a real (if thin) evidence report
4	with zero keys and zero network. Real deterministic checks (DOI resolution,
5	metadata, dedup) are Nick's, in ``slopchecker.checks`` (#8+), registered
6	against the same decorator.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from slopchecker.models import FlattenedDoc, LedgerRow
12	from slopchecker.pipeline.registry import CheckContext, CheckOutput, register
13	
14	
15	@register(
16	    id="has_text",
17	    name="Document has extractable text",
18	    tier="deterministic",
19	    timeout_s=5.0,
20	)
21	def has_text(doc: FlattenedDoc, ctx: CheckContext) -> CheckOutput:
22	    """False for an empty/whitespace-only text layer — the classic scanned-PDF gap."""
23	    ok = bool(doc.text.strip())
24	    return CheckOutput(
25	        ledger=[
26	            LedgerRow(
27	                check="has_text",
28	                label="Document has extractable text",
29	                result=ok,
30	                detail=None if ok else "no text layer — most checks have nothing to read",
31	            )
32	        ]
33	    )
34	
35	
36	@register(
37	    id="word_count",
38	    name="Word count",
39	    tier="deterministic",
40	    timeout_s=5.0,
41	)
42	def word_count(doc: FlattenedDoc, ctx: CheckContext) -> CheckOutput:
43	    """A number in the score lane, not a pass/fail — length is context, not a verdict."""
44	    n = len(doc.text.split())
45	    return CheckOutput(
46	        ledger=[LedgerRow(check="word_count", label="Word count", result=n, detail="words")]
47	    )
48

content.text: Found it — there's now an actual issue: **#90**, filed by Emerson, specifically for handling rubrics (arrival/storage/ingest of funder RFP + scoring documents). It didn't exist when I searched earlier. Let me pull it up to correct the record.

{"number":90,"title":"Rubrics: upload, store, and ingest funder reference docs","body":"## What a "rubric" is

Team term, settled 2026-07-31: a **rubric** is the funder-side reference document set a submission is checked against — the solicitation/RFP text, evaluation criteria and weights, program priorities, formatting and eligibility requirements. This is the thing we'd been loosely calling "reference docs."

Explicitly *not* rubrics (they already have homes):
- Cited-source texts for quote/citation verification — that's `SourceFetcher` (#10, #11).
- The prior-submission corpus for similarity — that's #14.

## Why

Three parts of the tool already assume reference material exists, and none of them define how it arrives:
- #16 (solicitation compliance) consumes a solicitation spec but has no path for the underlying document to enter the system.
- The web layer (#27) accepts exactly one upload: the submission itself.
- The CLI has no rubric argument.

## Architecture strawman

1. **Rubrics are ordinary documents.** They enter through the existing ingest layer (#4) → `FlattenedDoc`. No new parser, no special format — funders hand us PDFs.
2. **Storage:** shared and demo rubrics live in R2 under `slopchecker-docs/rubrics/` (synthetic fixtures under `rubrics/synthetic/`); the fabricated markdown sources stay in the repo at `fixtures/rubrics/`. `docs/data-storage.md` table updated as keys land. (Note: `harness/fixtures/` is deliberately NOT the home — the harness mutates and checks everything in that directory, so a rubric there would get scored as a proposal.)
3. **CLI:** `slopcheck run --rubric `; later maybe an R2 key for shared rubrics.
4. **Web:** optional second multipart field `rubric` on `POST /check` — coordinated with #27, where the web layer is actively moving today.
5. **Relationship to #16:** the YAML spec is the *compiled* form of a rubric. Pipeline: rubric doc (the human artifact) → LLM-drafted spec → human review → deterministic checks. This issue owns arrival, storage, and ingest of the doc; #16 keeps the spec format and the checks themselves.
6. **Degrade to gaps:** no rubric supplied → rubric-dependent checks report coverage gaps, never crash (house rule).

## Plan

- [x] Synthetic rubric fixtures, fabricated per the #22 rule: 2–3 realistic funder docs (an RFP with formatting/budget/eligibility rules; a weighted evaluation-criteria rubric), markdown source + PDF render — landed in PR #92, `fixtures/rubrics/`
- [x] Upload to R2 `rubrics/synthetic/`, document in `docs/data-storage.md` — 6 objects, verified 2026-07-31
- [x] Verify they ingest cleanly (text layer, section structure) through `ingest.ingest()` — see PR #92; PDF loader caveat below
- [ ] `--rubric` CLI plumbing
- [ ] Web upload slot (with #27)
- [ ] Spec-drafting bridge to #16

# SlopChecker

An open-source utility for funding orgs to screen incoming proposals for
AI-generation signals, citation integrity, solicitation compliance, and
tagging. It reports evidence for a human reviewer — it never auto-rejects
anything.

Built by a five-person team at [Hacking the Think Tank](https://hackingthethinktank.com/)
(2026-07-31).

## Quickstart

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker.git
cd SlopChecker
pip install -e ".[dev,pdf,docx]"
cp .env.example .env          # optional — every key is optional, see below
slopcheck run harness/fixtures/proposal_climate.md --tier deterministic
```

That runs the checks that need no API keys and no network, and writes
`slopcheck-reports/proposal_climate.report.json` (+ `.html` if you add
`--format json,html`). Add `--tier all` once you've filled in `.env` to
also run the API/LLM-backed checks.

```bash
slopcheck --help          # commands: run, render, config, version
slopcheck run --help      # --tier, --only/--skip, --format, --dry-run, --batch
slopcheck config          # shows which API keys are set, without printing them
```

`slopcheck render report.json --pdf` turns a `report.json` into the
paginated PDF evidence report — the actual shipping artifact; HTML is the
design-fidelity preview.

## API keys

Every key in `.env.example` is optional. A check whose key is missing
reports `skipped: missing <VAR>` instead of crashing the run — see
`slopcheck config` to check what's set.

## How it's organized

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/slopchecker/pipeline/` | check registry, tiered runner, citation extraction |
| `src/slopchecker/lenses/` | LLM prompt packs (markdown, see [`lenses/README.md`](src/slopchecker/lenses/README.md)) |
| `src/slopchecker/detect/` | AI-detection providers (Pangram) |
| `src/slopchecker/checks/` | deterministic checks: DOI resolution, metadata, tagging |
| `src/slopchecker/report/` | evidence report rendering: HTML + PDF |
| `src/slopchecker/ingest/` | PDF/DOCX/MD/HTML → normalized `FlattenedDoc` |
| `worker/` | Cloudflare Worker proxy + landing page |
| `harness/` | planted-defect validation, recall scoring |
| `fixtures/`, `tests/fixtures/` | fabricated test documents — never real applicant material (#22) |

`report.json` is the contract between checks and the renderer — see
[`docs/DATA_MODEL.md`](docs/DATA_MODEL.md) for the schema, a worked
example, and how to run the tests. Shared bulk data (corpora, fixtures too
big for git) lives in Cloudflare R2 — see
[`docs/data-storage.md`](docs/data-storage.md) for what's there and how to
get access.

## Contributing

See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get set up, and
[`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for the full set of team conventions (module
ownership, git discipline, design decisions already made).

## Team

Nick Wagner, Dan Parshall, Emerson Brooking, Alex, Dominique Ramsawak —
see `CLAUDE.md` for GitHub handles.

# Contributing

This is a hackathon project (five people, one week) — the process below
is meant to reduce collisions, not gatekeep. Full team conventions,
module ownership, and design decisions already made live in
[`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md); this file is the shorter "how do I get set up
and land my first change" version. If the two ever disagree, `CLAUDE.md`
wins.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,pdf,docx]"    # add ,llm ,web ,harness as needed
cp .env.example .env                # optional — see README's "API keys"
ruff check .
pytest
```

## Pick up work

1. **Start from an open issue** — the issue tree (#2–#25, plus later
   ones) is the work plan. Check `CLAUDE.md`'s module ownership table
   first if the issue touches someone else's module.
2. **Comment on the issue when you start** ("Claiming — ...") so two
   people don't collide, and comment again when you finish with what
   landed and the PR link.
3. **One branch per unit of work:** `<handle>/<issue#>-<slug>`, e.g.
   `nick/8-doi-resolution`.
4. **Reference the issue number** in commits and the PR title (`#19`).

## Before opening a PR

- Run the tests you touched, at minimum. `pytest -m integration` runs the
  slower full-CLI-chain suite separately (skipped by default).
- `ruff check .`
- Rebase on `main`: `git pull --rebase origin main`, resolve conflicts,
  force-push your branch (never `main` — direct pushes to `main` are
  rejected; branch force-push is fine).
- Append a line to `STATUS.md`'s `## Log` (newest on top) and, for any
  substantive AI session, add `ai-log/YYYY-MM-DD-<handle>-<slug>.md`
  covering what changed, decisions made and why, and dead ends hit.

## Merging

Small PRs merge fast; big ones rot. Review is welcome but not required —
if no one bites within a few minutes, merge your own PR. Squash-merge,
delete the branch.

## Ground rules worth repeating here

- **Check results are `true | false | number`, never free text** — see
  `docs/DATA_MODEL.md`. A checker that can't express its finding as a
  bool or a score is doing too much.
  Scores are evidence, never verdicts — the tool recommends
  `human_review`, it never auto-rejects.
- **Every finding is quote-anchored** — mechanically grounded in the
  source text before it reaches the report.
- **Degrade to gaps, never crash.** Missing API key, paywalled source, no
  text layer: record it as a coverage gap and continue.
- **Fixtures are fabricated, always.** No real applicant material in the
  test corpus, ever (#22).
- **Changing a shared model** (`src/slopchecker/models.py`) — comment on
  #3 first; everything downstream breaks silently otherwise.

## Attribution

Commits should carry a real, attributable identity — not a generic bot
identity — so `git log` and GitHub both show who produced the change:
`git config user.name "Name (surface)"` (e.g. `"Nick (claude-code)"`) with
your real email. AI-authored or co-authored commits also carry a
`Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming the model. See `CLAUDE.md` for the full
rationale, including the session-transcript logging setup.

AI-generation signals, citation integrity, solicitation compliance, and
tagging. It reports evidence for a human reviewer — it never auto-rejects
anything.

Built by a five-person team at [Hacking the Think Tank](https://hackingthethinktank.com/)
(2026-07-31).

## Quickstart

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker.git
cd SlopChecker
pip install -e ".[dev,pdf,docx]"
cp .env.example .env          # optional — every key is optional, see below
slopcheck run harness/fixtures/proposal_climate.md --tier deterministic
```

`slopcheck-reports/proposal_climate.report.json` (+ `.html` if you add

also run the API/LLM-backed checks.

slopcheck run --help      # --tier, --only/--skip, --format, --dry-run, --batch

# SlopChecker An open-source utility for funding orgs to screen incoming proposals for AI-generation signals, citation integrity, solicitation compliance, and tagging. It reports evidence for a human reviewer — it never auto-rejects anything. Built by a five-person team at [Hacking the Think Tank](https://hackingthethinktank.com/) (2026-07-31). ## Quickstart ```bash git clone https://github.com/nawagner/SlopChecker.git cd SlopChecker pip install -e ".[dev,pdf,docx]" cp .env.example .env # optional — every key is optional, see below slopcheck run harness/fixtures/proposal_climate.md --tier deterministic ``` That runs the checks that need no API keys and no network, and writes `slopcheck-reports/proposal_climate.report.json` (+ `.html` if you add `--format json,html`). Add `--tier all` once you've filled in `.env` to also run the API/LLM-backed checks. ```bash slopcheck --help # commands: run, render, config, version slopcheck run --help # --tier, --only/--skip, --format, --dry-run, --batch slopcheck config # shows which API keys are set, without printing them ``` `slopcheck render report.json --pdf` turns a `report.json` into the paginated PDF evidence report — the actual shipping artifact; HTML is the design-fidelity preview. ## API keys Every key in `.env.example` is optional. A check whose key is missing reports `skipped: missing ` instead of crashing the run — see `slopcheck config` to check what's set. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Proposal
PDF / DOCX / MD / HTML"] --> B["ingest/
normalize to text"] B --> C["FlattenedDoc"] C --> D["pipeline runner
--tier deterministic | api | llm | all"] D --> D1["checks/
deterministic
(DOI, metadata, tagging)"] D --> D2["detect/
api
(Pangram)"] D --> D3["lenses/
llm
(claim extraction, ...)"] D1 --> E["EvidenceReport
report.json"] D2 --> E D3 --> E E --> F["render/"] F --> G["HTML report"] F --> H["PDF report
(shipping artifact)"] ``` Every check result feeding into `report.json` is `true | false | number` plus a `skipped`/`errored` status — never free text, never a verdict. See [`docs/DATA_MODEL.md`](docs/DATA_MODEL.md) for the full contract. ## How it's organized | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `src/slopchecker/pipeline/` | check registry, tiered runner, citation extraction | | `src/slopchecker/lenses/` | LLM prompt packs (markdown, see [`lenses/README.md`](src/slopchecker/lenses/README.md)) | | `src/slopchecker/detect/` | AI-detection providers (Pangram) | | `src/slopchecker/checks/` | deterministic checks: DOI resolution, metadata, tagging | | `src/slopchecker/report/` | evidence report rendering: HTML + PDF | | `src/slopchecker/ingest/` | PDF/DOCX/MD/HTML → normalized `FlattenedDoc` | | `worker/` | Cloudflare Worker proxy + landing page | | `harness/` | planted-defect validation, recall scoring | | `fixtures/`, `tests/fixtures/` | fabricated test documents — never real applicant material (#22) | `report.json` is the contract between checks and the renderer — see [`docs/DATA_MODEL.md`](docs/DATA_MODEL.md) for the schema, a worked example, and how to run the tests. Shared bulk data (corpora, fixtures too big for git) lives in Cloudflare R2 — see [`docs/data-storage.md`](docs/data-storage.md) for what's there and how to get access. ## Contributing See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get set up, and [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for the full set of team conventions (module ownership, git discipline, design decisions already made). ## Team Nick Wagner, Dan Parshall, Emerson Brooking, Alex, Dominique Ramsawak — see `CLAUDE.md` for GitHub handles.

Closes #24.

## Summary
- **README.md**: real project description, live-demo link ([slop-checker.com](https://slop-checker.com), #27), a verified quickstart (install → run against a fabricated fixture → render), a mermaid diagram of the ingest → tiered checks → report → render pipeline, and a pointer map to the package layout and docs (`DATA_MODEL.md`, `data-storage.md`, `lenses/README.md`).
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** (new): short onboarding path — setup, how to pick up an issue, PR checklist, attribution — that defers to `CLAUDE.md` for the full policy rather than duplicating it.
- **.gitignore**: added `slopcheck-reports/`, the CLI's actual default output folder name, which the existing `reports/` rule didn't match — every fresh quickstart run was leaving an untracked directory.

Every command in the README was actually run against `harness/fixtures/proposal_climate.md` to confirm it works as documented (install, `slopcheck run --tier deterministic`, default output path, `slopcheck --help`/`run --help`/`config`).

## Test plan
- [x] `ruff check .` — passes
- [x] Ran the documented quickstart end-to-end (install, `slopcheck run harness/fixtures/proposal_climate.md --tier deterministic`, confirmed default `slopcheck-reports/` output)
- [x] No code changes — docs/config only, no test suite impact
